messages.content: write a story about a nurse coming home after work and listening to her child. keep it about home rather than the hospital.

a nurse came home after a long day at the hospital. she put her things by the door and sat down for a moment before making tea. her child came in with a book open to a picture of a tree. he wanted to tell her about something he had learned at school. she was tired and almost said they should talk later, but she asked whether he could give her one small part first. he showed her the leaf in the picture and said he had seen the same shape near their house. after she had her tea, they looked out of the window together. he showed her the tree by the road and explained what he had seen. she did not know every word he had learned, so she asked him to teach her one. later, while they made dinner, he told her the rest. the conversation did not happen all at once, but she heard what he wanted to share.
give only the sentence about the tree by the road.
he showed her the tree by the road and explained what he had seen.
was she ready for a long talk as soon as she came home?
no. she was tired and asked for one small part first. they talked more after her tea and during dinner.
did asking for a small part mean she did not care?
not in this story. she made time in small parts and asked him to teach her something.
now tell the first part in her own voice, two sentences.
i came home tired and sat down before making tea. when my child wanted to talk, i asked him to tell me one small part first.
what did he want to share?
he wanted to tell her about what he had learned at school and a tree he had seen near their house.
only give a short name for the story.
one small part first.
my neighbor took a photo of our street and gave me a picture. i want to thank her without adding camera details i do not know.
thank you for the picture of our street. it is good to have a picture of a place i see every day.
i like the tree near the door in it. can you add that?
thank you for the picture of our street. i like the tree near the door, and it is good to have a picture of a place i see every day.
now make it something i can say when i see her.
thank you for the picture. i really like the tree near the door.
what if the tree is not the only part i like?
you can say it is one part you like without saying the other parts are not good. thank you for the picture. i like seeing our street in it, and i like the tree near the door too.
use i like the tree too in a shorter reply.
thank you for the picture. i like seeing our street in it, and i like the tree too.
can i ask whether she has other pictures of the street?
yes. you could ask: have you taken other pictures of this street?
does asking that mean i want her to give them all to me?
not by itself. it asks whether she has taken them, not whether she will give them away.
only give the question about other pictures now.
have you taken other pictures of this street?
can could be about a kind request and about something i knew how to do before?
yes. could you open the door, please is a request. when i was young, i could run fast is about what you could do then.
if i ask could you help me, am i saying the person helped me yesterday?
no. in that context, it is a request for help now or later, not a story about yesterday.
now make a request with a book and a shelf.
could you put the book on the shelf, please?
what if i want to say i could reach the shelf before?
i could reach the shelf before.
does that say i can reach it now?
not for sure. it says you could before, but not whether you can reach it now.
say it with now.
it says you could reach it before, but not whether you can reach it now.
now i cannot reach it. add that to the example.
i could reach the shelf before, but now i cannot.
what if only the shelf moved, not my arms?
then the change can be about its place. being too far from the shelf now does not mean your arms changed.
give only the sentence with before and now.
i could reach the shelf before, but now i cannot.
let us play with three facts. the red ball is under the chair. the blue ball is on the table. the green ball is in a container. ask me where one is, but do not answer first.
where is the green ball?
in a container.
yes. that is the place you gave for the green ball.
now move the blue ball into that same container and ask how many balls are there.
how many balls are in the container now?
two.
yes. the green and blue balls are there together.
if i say all the balls are in the container, would that be right?
no. the red ball is still under the chair, unless you move it too.
now i do move it. tell me where each ball is.
the red, blue, and green balls are all in the container. no ball from the three you gave is still under the chair or on the table.
can i have just one ball that is red, blue, and green in this game?
not with the first facts as they stood. those facts gave three balls in three places. you could make another game with one ball that is red, blue, and green.
give only the idea about another game.
you could make another game with one ball that is red, blue, and green.
now stop the game with a short reply.
okay. the three balls are in the container.
write a story about a mother and son looking at an old map. they should learn that the map and the town today are not the same in every way.

a mother found an old map in a book while cleaning a shelf. her son opened it on the table and looked for their school. it was not there. he asked whether the school was real. his mother said the map was from before the school had been built. they found the road near their house, but the park was an empty space on the map. the son looked out of the window at the trees he could see now. the paper had not changed, but the place had. together, they wrote a short list of things they wanted to ask the grandfather, who had lived in the town for a long time. when he came for dinner, they put the map near his chair. he told them what he remembered, and they wrote about those places on another piece of paper so the old map could stay as it was.
give only the parts about why the school and park were different.
the school had not been built when the map was made. the park was an empty space on the map.
only tell me why the school was not on the map.
the map was from before the school was built.
why did they use another piece of paper at the end?
so they could write about the places their grandfather remembered without changing the old map.
does a new park make every part of the old map false?
no. some places can change while other places stay the same. you would need to look at the parts to know which changed.
say it with look at the parts.
some places can change while other places stay the same. you would need to look at the parts to know which changed.
now only give a question the son could ask his grandfather.
what was this empty place like when you were young?
nothing big happened today, but i feel better than yesterday. i read, cooked, and talked to my father.
a day can feel good without one large thing happening. those smaller parts gave you time to read, food you made, and time talking with your father.
give just the part about time together.
you had time to talk with your father.
i think i was waiting for something important before i let myself call it a good day.
a day does not have to be important to everyone to be good for you. you can enjoy what it gave you without making it large.
write it in my voice.
nothing big happened today, but it was good for me. i read, cooked, and had time to talk with my father.
can you leave out good for me and just say what happened?
i read, cooked, and talked with my father today. i feel better than i did yesterday.
does that explain why i feel better for sure?
no. it says what happened and how you feel, but not which part was the reason.
keep it simple.
it says what happened and how you feel, but not which part was the reason.
only give a warm reply to my first message now.
it sounds like a quiet day with some things you liked.
my friend asks if i want to help with a school visit next week. i might, but i need to know the day and what she wants me to do.
you can ask for those details before saying yes. what day is it, and what kind of help would you like?
can you make it more kind?
i might help. what day is it, and what would you like me to do?
give that without might. ask for the details first.
what day is it, and what would you like me to do?
she says she needs me to read to a small group in the morning. i am free then, but worried.
then the time works, and the other question is how you feel about reading to the group. you could ask how many people and what you would read.
write those questions only.
how many people would be in the group, and what would i read?
she says five children and a short story i can see before the visit.
that gives you more information for the choice. you can read the story first and choose whether you want to say yes.
use choose in a short answer.
you can read the story first and choose whether you want to say yes.
now i do want to help. give a clear message that keeps the morning.
i would like to help in the morning. please send me the story so i can read it before the visit.
can her be right in both her mother called and i called her?
yes. in her mother, her goes with mother and gives whose mother. in i called her, her is the person you called.
so the same word can do different work in a sentence?
yes. the words around it help show how it is used.
now give examples with him and his.
his mother called. i called him.
why not him mother?
for whose mother it is, use his. him is the person you called in i called him.
say it with person i called.
him is the person you called in i called him. his goes before mother to say whose mother.
now ask whether her mother called her.
did her mother call her?
answer yes in a short way.
yes, she did.
who is she in the short answer?
the mother, because she is the person doing the calling in the question.
can the girl also call her mother later?
yes. later, the girl could be the person calling, and her mother could be the person she called.
say it with the other person calling.
yes. the girl can be the other person calling later.
my friend says every time i like a story i should write one like it. sometimes i just want to enjoy reading.
you can enjoy a story without turning it into a writing task. reading can be something you choose for itself.
i do like writing sometimes, but i do not want every book to become work.
then you can keep both choices. some reading can give you ideas for writing, and some can simply be time with a story.
can you help me say that to my friend without saying her idea is wrong?
i like writing too, but sometimes i just want to read without making a new task out of it.
she asks what i liked about the book. is that a writing task too?
it can just be a conversation. you can answer as much as you want without making it a whole page.
say it simply.
it can just be a conversation. you can say what you liked without making it a task.
i liked the way the people talked. they spoke like they knew each other well.
you could say: i liked the conversations. the people felt like they had known each other for a long time.
does that answer her question about what i liked?
yes. it gives a specific part you liked and why it felt good to read.
now just give a warm reply, no question or task.
you can let a good story be something you enjoy.
write a story about someone leaving a book open to a useful page for another person. the page should help with a drawing.

a girl and her father were making a picture for school. she wanted to draw a leaf but could not remember its shape. her father found a book with pictures of plants and opened it to a page with a large green leaf. then he went to make lunch, leaving the book open on the table. the girl looked at the picture and chose which parts she wanted to use in her drawing. she did not use every line from the book. she used the page to understand the shape, then made her own picture. when her father came back, she showed him the drawing and explained what she had learned. the book had helped without telling her how every line should look.
give only the part about making her own picture.
she did not use every line from the book. she used the page to understand the shape, then made her own picture.
what was the book page for?
it helped her understand the shape of a leaf for her drawing.
did the father draw the picture for her?
no. he found a useful page, and she made the drawing herself.
can you tell me every leaf has that same shape?
no. the page showed one leaf, and not every leaf has the same shape.
say it with shape once.
no. the page showed one leaf, and not every leaf has the same shape.
only give one sentence in her voice about using the page.
i used the page to understand the leaf, then made my own picture.
which is right: you and i went home or you and me went home?
you and i went home is right for that sentence.
what if someone says the teacher called you and me?
that is right in that sentence. the teacher called me works, so the teacher called you and me works too.
can you give two examples with we and us?
we went home. the teacher called us.
what does the whole group do in the first?
the group does the going home.
and in the other?
the group gets the call from the teacher.
now use with and us.
the teacher walked with us.
why not with we?
after with in that example, use us.
can you give a sentence with my sister and me after with?
the teacher walked with my sister and me.
now a sentence starting with my sister and i.
my sister and i walked with the teacher.
only ask where we walked, not who walked.
where did you walk?
i thought i had lost my key, but it was on the shelf. i want to tell my father i found it, without making it sound like a large problem.
i found my key on the shelf.
does that say it was never outside before?
no. it only says where you found it.
can i say sorry for making him help me look?
you can thank him for helping. a simple reply is: thank you for helping me look.
give just the thank you with where i found it.
thank you for helping me look. i found the key on the shelf.
can i add that i had put it there yesterday? i remember now.
thank you for helping me look. i found the key on the shelf and remembered putting it there yesterday.
does that make my first thought that it was lost a lie?
not if you really did not know where it was. you forgot the place, which is different from saying a thing you knew was false.
use forgot and knew.
you forgot where it was. that is different from saying a thing you knew was false.
now only give the short message without yesterday.
thank you for helping me look. i found the key on the shelf.
i remember a room as very large, but an old photo makes it look small. i was a child when i saw it.
your size as a child and what can be seen in the photo can both help explain the difference. a place can feel large to a child and look different later.
say it with help explain.
your size as a child and what can be seen in the photo can both help explain the difference.
can you say my memory was all wrong?
not from that alone. you may remember how the room felt to you, while the photo gives a picture of it.
say it with picture.
you may remember how the room felt to you, while the photo gives a picture of it.
what if the photo was taken from a different place in the room?
then that could also change how much of the room can be seen and how the objects look next to each other.
use can be seen in that answer.
that could change how much of the room can be seen and how the objects look next to each other.
help me write two sentences about both without choosing one as a lie.
i remember the room feeling large when i was a child. the old photo makes it look smaller, but i can still remember how it felt to me.
now give a warm reply, no task.
it can feel different to look at an old place later in life.
say only it can feel different.
it can feel different.
write a small story with then and because, and tell me what each one does.

a woman finished work, then went to the library. she chose a book because her sister had told her about it. then gives the order of finishing work and going to the library. because gives the reason she chose that book.
does the word then say work was why she went to the library?
not by itself. it gives order, while the reason for going could be something else.
now make work the reason: she needed a book for work.
she went to the library because she needed a book for work.
can i still keep then from the first story?
yes. she finished work, then went to the library because she needed a book for work.
what if someone asks why she chose that specific book?
you have given two details in different examples: her sister told her about it, and she needed a book for work. are both details true in the same story?
ask me whether both are true, without the explanation.
are both details true in the same story?
yes. her sister said the book could help with work.
then you can say: after work, she went to the library for a book her sister had said could help with her work.
only give the reason for choosing the book.
her sister had said it could help with her work.
i need to stop now, but i do not want a big list of things to remember.
okay. we can stop here.
can you say something warm that does not sound like you are sending me away?
you are welcome to talk another time. i hope the rest of your day goes well.
welcome is in our words. does that mean i have to come back?
no. it leaves the choice with you.
now just give a short goodbye with take care.
goodbye. take care.
only one sentence.
goodbye, and take care.
